thread:
zoe: quick flag  rolled orion-ptq-v2 (int8-ish PTQ) into streaming canary. parse failures for funcalls jumped to ~1.1% on the last 2k streamed calls.

karl: streaming or batch? any example snippets?

zoe: streaming. common pattern is truncated JSON suffixes and occasional trailing commas. pasted one sample from raw chunks:
```
{"action":"create_alert","params":{"title":"mem spike","hosts":["db1","db2",],"severity":"high"}
# stream ended mid-chunk
```

maya: that trailing comma + cut is classic chunk-boundary chop. how does fp16 look?

zoe: fp16-streaming baseline is ~0.03%. orion-ptq batch-mode = 0.15%. streaming + PTQ is the outlier.

samir: hypotheses: (A) quantized decoder changes tokenization leading to a mid-token cut, (B) transport framing is chopping multi-byte tokens differently under the new runtime, or (C) KV cache flush alignment interacts with streaming chunks. need to localize.

karl: urgent mitigations: 1) pause production streaming rollout for orion-ptq-v2; 2) enable a streaming "assembler" that buffers until syntactically-closed JSON or TTL=150ms; 3) disable auto-retry-on-parse-fail in canary to avoid duplicate tool invocations.

maya: adding a lightweight stitcher that only auto-fixes obvious final-token issues (trim trailing commas, append single missing brace if counts off by 1). tag anything repaired with metadata so we don't count it as a true parse_fail.

zoe: good. also queue a mirror job: mirror orion-ptq-v2 streaming -> fp16 streaming for 5k samples so we can diff per-token checksums.

canary-bot: queued mirror job: /ci/mirror/1777771234 (5k). will post results to /ci/reports/1777771234-mirror.json.

samir: also instrument per-chunk sha256 and last-8-bytes to catch partial-UTF8 or partial-escape sequences. if raw bytes differ before decoding between fp16 and PTQ, it's generation-level. if bytes same but decoded text differs, it's decoding/transport.

karl: quick repro harness snippet (for visibility):
```python
from redwood_client import Client
c = Client(model="orion-ptq-v2", stream=True, seed=1337, temp=0.0)
for p in load_prompts('toolcall-heavy'):
  r = c.generate(p)
  dump_raw_chunks(r.raw_bytes)  # save raw bytes & token indices
```

maya: minor UX: set assembler to only buffer when last chunk lacks any closing brace/bracket and ends in non-whitespace. that'll avoid buffering most short responses and keep latency low. TTL start=150ms.

samir: if mirror report shows checksum divergence at token < 40, we treat as kernel/quant distortion and run per-layer rollback: mixed-precision last-8..last-1. will run a 8-job sweep and report parse_failure_rate + p95 latency + cost delta.

canary-bot: mirror report posted: /ci/reports/1777771234-mirror.json (parse_fail_streaming:1.12%, buffered:0.13%, fp16-streaming:0.03%, checksum_divergence_median_token:45).

karl: divergence token ~45 -> generation-level. start quant ablation. samir take ownership.

samir: starting ablation grid: variants = [per-channel-scale, last-4-mixed-precision, clamp-adjust, per-tensor]. running small 1k jobs. will post results.

zoe: I've paused streaming rollout and switched canary to buffered-mode until we have a fix. created ticket INF-4220 and assigned to @samir and @karl.

maya: thanks. stitcher + no-retry kept duplicate-invokes down in the short term so at least customer-visible throttles are sane. follow-up once ablation numbers land. :thumbsup:
